cve_summary: A flaw was found in the hugetlb_mcopy_atomic_pte function in mm/hugetlb.c in the Linux kernel before 4.13. A superfluous implicit page unlock for VM_SHARED hugetlbfs mapping could trigger a local denial of service (BUG).
commit_message:
userfaultfd: hugetlbfs: remove superfluous page unlock in VM_SHARED case

huge_add_to_page_cache->add_to_page_cache implicitly unlocks the page
before returning in case of errors.

The error returned was -EEXIST by running UFFDIO_COPY on a non-hole
offset of a VM_SHARED hugetlbfs mapping.  It was an userland bug that
triggered it and the kernel must cope with it returning -EEXIST from
ioctl(UFFDIO_COPY) as expected.

  page dumped because: VM_BUG_ON_PAGE(!PageLocked(page))
  kernel BUG at mm/filemap.c:964!
  invalid opcode: 0000 [#1] SMP
  CPU: 1 PID: 22582 Comm: qemu-system-x86 Not tainted 4.11.11-300.fc26.x86_64 #1
  RIP: unlock_page+0x4a/0x50
  Call Trace:
    hugetlb_mcopy_atomic_pte+0xc0/0x320
    mcopy_atomic+0x96f/0xbe0
    userfaultfd_ioctl+0x218/0xe90
    do_vfs_ioctl+0xa5/0x600
    SyS_ioctl+0x79/0x90
    entry_SYSCALL_64_fastpath+0x1a/0xa9

docstring:
/******************************************************************************  
 * Summary:  
 * This function atomically copies a huge page table entry from a source address  
 * to a destination address in a specified memory management structure.  
 *  
 * Parameters:  
 * dst_mm (struct mm_struct *): The destination memory management structure.  
 * dst_pte (pte_t *): Pointer to the destination page table entry.  
 * dst_vma (struct vm_area_struct *): The destination virtual memory area.  
 * dst_addr (unsigned long): The destination address for the page.  
 * src_addr (unsigned long): The source address from which to copy the page.  
 * pagep (struct page **): Pointer to a page pointer for the copied page.  
 *  
 * Returns:  
 * int: Returns 0 on success, or a negative error code on failure.  
 *  
 * Logic:  
 * The function allocates a huge page if none is provided, copies data from the  
 * user space, updates the page state, and sets the page table entry. It handles  
 * shared and private mappings differently and ensures proper locking and  
 * memory barriers are in place to maintain consistency.  
 ******************************************************************************/
